morning.text: Morning! Busy night on the platforms. A locket, a briefcase, a rabbit, two of nearly everything.
Oh, and there's a watch in drawer D that I don't like the look of. Have a squint at its tag before you do anything with it.
That photograph came in last night, the one of you. Put it in a frame, I did. Gave me the shivers.
Yesterday's page is in the ledger on your desk, if you want to look back. Agnes always did, first thing.

Two today, love. Some days there are two people for every one thing.

And if a tall gentleman in grey comes to the window: smile, say no, and mean it.

intro.text: Good morning! Constable Bramble, station police. I've come about an umbrella.
{Green, with a duck's head for a handle|umbrella}. Left it on {Platform 5|where} on Sunday evening, chasing a pickpocket.
My name's on it, mind. {Under the strap|name}. Can't be too careful, in my line of work.

claims.text: A green umbrella with a duck's-head handle
His name is written under the strap

answers.text: B. Bramble. Bartholomew, but don't spread it about.
Chipped it on a pickpocket's noggin, Whitsun. He came quietly after that.

notMine.text: That's not it, I'm afraid. Green, duck's head. Can't miss it.

missing.text: Gone? Handed to a gentleman in a kipper tie and a wide hat?
That'll be Reggie Stokes. Right. I'll be having a word with Mr Stokes.

cases.missingLedger: Reggie walked off with the Constable's umbrella yesterday. It wasn't here to return.

verdicts.ledger: The Constable knew his name was under the strap, and how the beak got chipped. Refusing Reggie yesterday paid off.

reply.text: That's the fellow! Much obliged. If anyone gives you trouble, you send for Bramble.

verdicts.ledger: His name was under the strap, just as he said. It was his.

reply.text: Refused? A police officer? Well. I'll be making a note of this.

verdicts.ledger: Just an umbrella. It should have gone home with the Constable.

reply.text: Locking it up? It's evidence of nothing, that brolly!

cases.hint: Two claimants? Each half of the slip is theirs. Stamp RETURN on the half of the one it belongs to.

intro.text: Good morning! We've come about our locket.
{Silver, with ivy on the front|silver}. Gran gave it to me. There's {a note inside that says "Happy birthday, Rosie"|note}.
It's {silver, with ivy|silver}, and it's mine. {Gran's picture is inside|photo}, and {a note she wrote for me|note}.
We lost it on Platform 3 last night. We do everything together.

claims.text: A silver locket with ivy on the front
The note inside says "Happy birthday, Rosie"
There's a note Gran wrote for her

answers.text: "For Cecily, who never loses anything." Gran was being funny.
Gran, in her Sunday hat. She hated that photo.

verdicts.ledger: Both twins could see the ivy, and both knew Gran's photo. Only Cecily knew what the note said: it had her name on it.

reply.text: Thank you. I knew someone would read it properly.
...I was only borrowing it.

verdicts.ledger: The note inside said "For Cecily". Rosalind got it wrong. The object decides.

reply.text: Ha! Told you.
You didn't even read it.

verdicts.ledger: The note named Cecily. When two people claim one thing, let the object decide.

reply.text: But it says my name!

verdicts.ledger: A family locket, nothing strange about it. It should have gone home with Cecily.

reply.text: Well, now neither of us has it.

intro.text: Ah. Good morning. Haversham. Hugo. I — I left my {briefcase|case} on a train. Leather.
Most important. Inside are {the ledgers for the Pemberton account|contents}. Very confidential. Columns, figures.
And my initials, of course. {H.H., in the lining|initials}.

claims.text: Ledgers for the Pemberton account inside
His initials, H.H., in the lining

answers.text: A sandwich? I never eat at my desk. Ulcer.

notMine.text: N-no, that's not it. Mine's a leather briefcase.

verdicts.ledger: No ledgers: a racing form and an egg-and-cress sandwich. The lining said D.F., not H.H.

reply.text: Ah. Well. Perhaps it was a different briefcase. Good day.

verdicts.ledger: There were no ledgers inside, and the lining said D.F. Hugo was lying.

reply.text: Oh! Oh, thank you. Thank you very much indeed.

verdicts.ledger: Nothing uncanny about a sandwich. It just wasn't his. Refuse him, and the owner will come.

reply.text: The — the safe? What on earth for?

intro.text: Good morning. You must be the new one. You have her eyes.
I've come for my watch. {Silver|watch}. {It runs backwards|hands}, which suits me very well.
{Station Master, Ninefold, engraved inside the lid|engraving}. You'll find everything exactly as I say. I am never wrong about my things.

answers.text: Backwards, yes. It's counting down. To what, I wonder?
Station Master, Ninefold. A position of some importance. Vacant, I believe.

verdicts.ledger: Mr Vell knew every detail, as he always does. But the tag said it was found on Wednesday: tomorrow. Things from tomorrow go in the Iron Drawer.

reply.text: The Iron Drawer. How very like her.
No matter. I'm a patient man. I'll be back on Thursday.

verdicts.ledger: Right to refuse Mr Vell: the Grey Gentleman gets nothing. But the watch came from tomorrow. It belonged in the Iron Drawer.

reply.text: No? Just like that? She trained you well.
I'll be back on Thursday.

verdicts.ledger: You gave the Grey Gentleman the Station Master's watch. Did the colours look a little thinner after he left?

reply.text: Thank you. Thank you so very much.
Tick, tock. Backwards.

intro.text: Hiya! Have you got Mr Hops? He's {a grey rabbit|rabbit}. He's not mine, he's my brother's, Tobi's.
Tobi left him on the {school train|where} yesterday and he's been crying ALL night. He's three.
{Tobi chews his ear|ear} when he's asleep. It's disgusting. Mum says it's a comfort.

claims.text: A grey toy rabbit called Mr Hops
Left on the school train, yesterday
Her brother chews one of his ears

answers.text: OKAFOR! That's us! Mum sews our name in everything, even my PE knickers.

notMine.text: That's not Mr Hops, silly. He's a rabbit!

verdicts.ledger: The chewed ear and the OKAFOR tag. Mr Hops went home to Tobi.

reply.text: MR HOPS! Tobi is going to go bananas!
Thanks, mister! I'll draw you something.

verdicts.ledger: Her name was sewn under his foot. Mr Hops should have gone home.

reply.text: But Tobi's CRYING.

verdicts.ledger: A toy rabbit isn't dangerous. He should have gone home to Tobi.

reply.text: You can't lock up Mr Hops! He hasn't done anything!

evening.text: That's your Tuesday. You're getting the hang of it.
Fellow in grey was asking about you, on the way out. Polite as anything. I didn't like it one bit.

gazette.headline: STATION CLOCKS RUN SLOW, SAY COMMUTERS
gazette.body: Passengers at Ninefold Junction report that the station clocks lost several minutes yesterday afternoon. Several also remarked that the paint seemed duller than they remembered.

gazette.headline: CONSTABLE REUNITED WITH TRUSTY BROLLY
gazette.body: Constable B. Bramble of the station police collected his umbrella from Lost Property yesterday. "Chipped the beak on a pickpocket," he told the Gazette. "Wouldn't swap it for a new one."

gazette.headline: TWINS IN PLATFORM 3 SQUABBLE
gazette.body: Commuters were treated to a lively exchange between the Misses Fairweather yesterday morning. The matter is understood to concern a locket, and their grandmother's handwriting.
